preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an autonomous or semi-autonomous coding agent performs substantive work in an ephemeral, inaccessible, or quota-dependent execution environment but postpones branch creation, commit, push, patch export, or equivalent durable checkpointing until after the expensive work is complete. If quota, session, infrastructure, authentication, tool, or task-state failure occurs before persistence, the completed work is lost and the user must repeat the task. The failure includes any workflow that reports or visibly presents substantive completion without ensuring that the resulting work product exists in a durable, user-accessible, resumable state.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met where a coding-agent task has produced substantive repository modifications or a materially complete work product, but no durable branch, commit, pushed patch, downloadable diff, archive, or resumable checkpoint exists before quota exhaustion or task failure; the user cannot recover the completed work; and repeating all or part of the task is required. Pull-request creation need not itself succeed for the threshold to be avoided, provided the completed work has already been durably preserved and can be manually reviewed or submitted.

preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: CAM distinguishes execution from successful completion, and completion from durable handoff. Repository work is not meaningfully complete while its result exists only inside an inaccessible or quota-dependent execution environment. Deferring branch creation, commit, push, or equivalent checkpointing until the end of a costly task creates an avoidable single point of failure. Where quota exhaustion prevents persistence, the platform converts a resource limit into irreversible work loss, duplicate computation, delayed delivery, and additional user cost. A governed coding agent should establish a durable work surface before substantive modification, checkpoint completed phases proportionately, reserve sufficient capacity for persistence and handoff, and provide a recoverable patch or branch even if pull-request creation cannot be completed.
